title: Microsoft Purview: collection policies can filter Insider Risk Management device signals
notes: claim 48: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the device collection policy precedence rule, licensing requirements and PowerShell command. The control path stops at the policy list, and the assertion that end users see nothing change is not documented.

claims.claim: Collection policies filter ingested events that can feed Purview solutions including IRM.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: File copied to removable media is a supported device collection policy activity.
claims.quote: File copied to removable media | When a file is copied to a removable media, such as a USB flash drive, on an onboarded endpoint device | Devices

claims.claim: Collection policies filter by the data source where the event happens, including devices.
claims.quote: A match to the data source or location where the event is happening. For example, a collection policy can be scoped to only collect events from devices

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A configured and deployed device collection policy takes precedence when its filtering conflicts with what an IRM policy monitors.
claims.quote: When a device collection policy is configured and deployed, if there's a conflict between what the Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor and what the collection policy is configured to filter for, the collection policy configuration takes precedence.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An activity monitored by IRM but filtered out by the device collection policy is not collected or available for IRM review.
claims.quote: if an Insider Risk Management policy is configured to monitor a specific activity, but the collection policy is configured to filter out that activity, the activity isn't collected and isn't available for review in Insider Risk Management.

claims.claim: IRM ignores a collected indicator that its policy is not configured for.
claims.quote: If a collection policy is configured to collect something that an Insider Risk Management policy isn't configured for, then the indicator is collected, but Insider Risk Management ignores it.

claims.claim: The documented IRM precedence effect applies only to device indicators.
claims.quote: This only applies to device indicators in Insider Risk Management policies, and only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented IRM precedence effect occurs only when a device collection policy is deployed.

claims.claim: Purview combines all collection policies for a data source into one policy during evaluation.
claims.quote: on the back end, during policy evaluation, Microsoft Purview combines all the collection policies for a data source into a single collection policy for that data source. So all the conditions for a data source are used when identifying matches.
